points.heading: Practice -ar
points.body:
Stay with the **-ar** family today. Remember: verb = action; conjugate = change for who; stem = fixed part; ending = tip. With **cantar**, drop **-ar** to keep **cant-**, then add **-o / -as / -a**.

Build a tiny story: yo **canto** in the morning, tú **cantas** at school, él **canta** at home. Switch the verb to **hablar** or **bailar** without changing the endings pattern.

Compare **canto** and **cantas** out loud: what stays (the stem) and what changes (the ending).

Compare two short examples out loud. Say what changes and what stays the same.

Write one sentence in your own words before you start the practice task.

Say the key idea without looking, then check whether any important detail is missing.

Teach this point to someone at home with a new example you invent.

Compare two short examples out loud. Say what changes and what stays the same.

Practice: Your turn. Write six forms: cantar and hablar for yo, tú, and él. Underline each ending.

Common mistake: Leaving -ar on the verb (yo cantaro). Always drop the infinitive ending first.

lesson.summary: In this lesson, you will use Spanish verb endings to say who does an action.
lesson.memoryPhrase: Spanish families: **-ar** (cantar → canto, cantas, canta), **-er** (comer → como, comes, come), **-ir** (vivir → vivo, vives, vive).
lesson.weekRecap: Spanish families: -ar (cantar), -er (comer), -ir (vivir). Conjugate for yo, tú, and él in the present.
